evidence: legacy_counts: CR is stripped per line, so CRLF pages now reach the legacy-key check; $unreadable is set when the opening or closing --- line has a CR, or when no closing --- is seen, and $bad is incremented only for pages with $legacy.
Both readers use the same line-ending strip, so a CRLF page now contributes to projects_of and to the per-project counts consistently.
The end-of-file edge cases, a closing --- with no trailing newline and a file that ends before any closing ---, are handled correctly by s/\r?\n\z// and by $closed.
$. is reset by close($h) between files, so the line-1 check is correct for every page.
I found no defect that this commit introduces. Whether the command really refuses an unclosed block cannot be checked from the diff alone.
